title: Build Python training harness and .NET bridge contract
description: Implement a reproducible local harness for SFT and preference tuning with .NET process orchestration, status contracts, and cancellation semantics.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from the staged harness architecture review; depends on transcript and export prerequisites.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Implemented first harness bridge slice with `Scripts/Run-FinetuneHarness.ps1` and `MemorySmith.Training/harness.py`, including request/status/event contract files and benchmark output. Executed run `sprint3-ft-20260528` with exported SFT JSONL, benchmark JSON, and pass/fail eval gate reporting.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Added dependency preflight (`Scripts/Test-FinetuneHarnessPrereqs.ps1`) and runner integration with optional fail-fast mode. Executed second benchmarked run `sprint8-ft-20260528` and revalidated full repo (`Scripts/Validate-Repo.ps1`: 419 tests, 0 failures). Remaining scope is true LoRA execution path once pinned training environment dependencies are provisioned.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Added in-app harness observability via `/training-workbench`: latest run phases, last events, elapsed seconds, record counts, and resolved `status.json` paths are now visible in Blazor without terminal access. This improves operational visibility while preserving existing script-first execution semantics.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Expanded workbench telemetry fidelity by parsing harness `events.jsonl` and `benchmark.json` artifacts for each run (last event timestamp, records/sec throughput, final loss, and latest event feed table). This closes the live telemetry visibility gap while keeping execution control script-first.
